value.rationale: An infinite family of finite trees with arbitrarily large branching supplies a strict log-concavity theorem, stronger than the affirmative unimodality sought by the motivating open tree question. The result counts all forcing sets rather than a minimum and derives a nontrivial inequality across every cardinality, with an explicit positive polynomial certificate. This is a natural graph family and coefficient-shape problem rather than an arbitrary small slice.
